title: Memory whirlpool: kv-cache backpressure and cross-tenant OOM recovery
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple production escalations across Hosted, Dedicated and Private customers surfaced a correlated failure mode we're calling the 'memory whirlpool': slow-growing GPU memory fragmentation combined with a KV cache backpressure spiral that causes long-tail OOMs and KV index corruption. Affected tenants include AcmePay (hosted), NovaDocs (dedicated), and MedixCloud (private/on-prem). The pattern: under sustained mixed-length Chat/Embedding workloads the runtime begins to evict and reallocate small slab sizes, triggering fragmentation. Eviction metadata races leave transient inconsistent KV index state; subsequent requests cause double-allocs and eventual GPU OOMs. Customers observed repeated session restarts, degraded latency, and 5xx error spikes. This ticket tracks investigation, the runtime patch (v2.4.1-alpha), and a staged canary rollout plus customer-facing mitigations.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime patch deployed to canary and no OOMs observed for 72h under synthetic mixed-length load
KV index corruption scan false-positive rate < 0.1% after reconciler fix
Affected customers agree degradation is resolved in their canaries and sign off for production rollout
Backfill telemetry showing eviction rate reduced and slab utilization variance decreased by >= 40%
steps_to_reproduce: Replay mixed Chat + Embedding workload using load-generator (scripts/loadmix.sh) at sustained 400 RPS with 1:4 short:long sequence ratio
Enable prefetched KV handles and set eviction threshold to 0.7 to reproduce fragmentation more quickly
Observe increasing slab allocation churn in grafana dashboard 'runtime/gpu/allocator/churn' and repeated KV handle rebuilds
Trigger background full-gc and verify OOM occurs within 40-90 minutes when race timing aligns
mitigation_actions: Short-term (customer-facing): throttle long sequences via rate-limiter rule, bump tenant qps weight down, and schedule rolling restarts for affected nodes -- communicated to customers with mitigation playbook
Medium-term: deploy runtime-2.4.1-alpha with KV index reconciler and conservative slab-coalescer (canary first)
Long-term: redesign allocation arena to reduce micro-slab churn and add stronger invariants on KV handle lifecycle with checksum + write-ahead tombstone
Operational: add a Grafana alert for sustained slab-variance > 0.6 and a tracing span that surfaces KV handle lock wait times
rollout_plan: 1) Validate unit + integration tests in CI (PR #1849) and run the benchmark harness with recorded customer traces
2) Canary deploy to 5% of Hosted and one Dedicated pool (staged during low-traffic window UTC 02:00-04:00)
3) Monitor for 72 hours: heap fragmentation, eviction rate, KV reconciler activity, and error rates; run forced traceback for two affected tenants
4) If stable, expand to 25% and then 100% over 48 hours with automated rollback if OOM rate > baseline
5) For Private/on-prem customers (MedixCloud), ship hotpatch package and assist their infra team with an assisted upgrade checklist
qa_notes: Create deterministic regression tests that seed eviction metadata races and validate KV index correctness after forced restarts
Include GPU memory stress tests with synthetic small-allocation patterns to exercise slab coalescer
Run end-to-end signing with AcmePay traces in staging and collect token-level latency histograms
